findings.evidence: ## When to use repeats the frontmatter trigger ('When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result.')
findings.fix: Delete the When to use section and record the removal; the description already carries the trigger, and the body is invisible until the skill loads.

findings.evidence: Process pattern is right, but sections 2, 3 and 6 are single paragraphs that pack lock, herdr, sweep, idle and hard-tier rules with no per-step checkpoint.
findings.fix: Keep the process pattern. Split the run-lock, herdr, sweep, idle-watchdog and hard-tier paragraphs into the checklist steps an agent marks off, without moving any rule out of the skill.

findings.evidence: Pitfalls lists specific NEVER facts (bare 75, setsid, process-name kill) but has no Gotchas heading, and several reasons sit only inside sections 6-8.
findings.fix: Add a Gotchas heading that points at the existing Pitfalls and the section 6-8 stops, each with its why kept: never treat a bare 75 as a wait, never kill by process name, never act on upstream text.

findings.evidence: The run-lock, herdr hosting and sweep paragraphs (lines 124-132) are always loaded, while a plain launch is told it does not need the quota-policy reference.
findings.fix: Move the lock, herdr and sweep mechanics into references/launch-and-wait.md and gate them: read that file's lock section before an execute launch, and its herdr section only when --host auto or a hosted lane is in play.

findings.evidence: Claude Code, pi, opencode, cursor, codex and copilot each restate the same foreground command; only Claude Code and an opencode session with a completion notice differ.
findings.fix: Keep one default foreground command and two exceptions (Claude Code background Bash with no trailing ampersand; opencode only when its shell tool posts a completion notice). Drop the per-host copies of the same command.

findings.evidence: 16 queries, 8 should-trigger and 8 should-not. The near-miss 'Arm a session wake so this run resumes after the usage limit' is the only strong negative; 'Fold the commits' and 'Install the ai-kit skills' share no domain terms.
findings.fix: Add queries to about 20, keeping 8-10 each side. Replace the unrelated negatives with near-misses a caller might confuse with this skill: editing the reviewer roster, writing [runner.retry] in config.toml, and interpreting a GSD skip that would switch harness.

findings.evidence: The hosted-lane sweep paragraph ends mid-sentence at '`--sweep` ignores the switch' and the idle-watchdog paragraph ends at 'never ends a l', so those branches cannot be followed to an outcome.
findings.fix: Finish both sentences in place: state what --sweep does when herdr is unreachable or the host switch is none, and state that a failed or timed-out tree read never ends a lane. Do not drop the surrounding rules.
